title: Microsoft 365 admin center: rules that automate agent lifecycle management

reasons: published before the check existed: kept live with a notice while a corrected version is prepared

summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly describes deletion as irreversible and omits the Agent Builder-only restriction on the manager-reassignment rule. It also treats administrator-run bulk rules as universally automatic and incorrectly says blocking is the only lifecycle action with an API. The roadmap metadata and the cited block endpoint are correct.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; What's changing; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The rule-creation path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > Agent management rules > Add rule.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to **Agents** > **Settings** > **Agent management rules**, and then select **Add rule**.

claims.claim: No API for creating or listing these Microsoft 365 admin center agent management rules is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "agent management rules" "API"; "agent management rules" "PowerShell"; Microsoft Graph agent management rules create list lifecycle rules API admin settings user access publish reject requests. Opened agent-settings and Package Management API overview; no matching rule API.

claims.claim: An individual agent can be blocked or unblocked through Agents > All agents > agent > Block / Unblock.
claims.quote:
Select **Agents** > **All agents**.
3. In the **All agents** page, select an agent from the list of agents.
4. In the agent details pane that opens, immediately under the agent's name, select **Block** or **Unblock**.
claims.fix: The pre-check's missing-word warning is cosmetic: Block and Unblock are documented. Narrow this row's governs label to 'Manual block or unblock for an agent'; the supplied path does not describe uninstalling or pinning.

claims.claim: POST /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package.
claims.quote:
Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block
claims.fix: Keep the endpoint, but label it preview/beta and block-only: it does not unblock, uninstall or pin. Add that production use is unsupported and that it requires delegated CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All; application permissions are unavailable.

claims.claim: Tenant agent access can be managed at Copilot > Settings > Data access > Agents.
claims.quote: Select **Copilot** > **Settings** > **Data access** > **Agents** to manage your organization's agents.
claims.fix: The cited guide supports the path. Note that https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-settings#user-access gives the newer route 'Agents > Settings > User access'; report both rather than silently choosing one.

claims.claim: No API equivalent of the tenant-wide agent user-access selector is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "agents" "user access" "PowerShell" Microsoft 365 admin center; "Copilot" "agent access" "Graph" tenant settings API. Opened agent-settings, the admin guide and Package Management API overview; found no API for this tenant selector.

claims.claim: Agent publish requests are approved or rejected under Agents > All agents > Requests > Publish / Reject.
claims.quote:
Select **Agents** > **All agents** > **Requests**.
3. Select the requested agent and view the agent's details.
4. Next to the name of the agent, select the action to **Publish** or **Reject** the agent.
claims.fix: Insert the omitted selection: 'Agents > All agents > Requests > agent > Publish / Reject'. The pre-check's missing words are present as separate labels. Also note https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-requests uses 'Publish to store' and 'Reject submission'.

claims.claim: An API for approving or rejecting these tenant agent publish requests is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "agent" "publish requests" "API" "reject" Microsoft 365; "agent publish" "approve" "Graph API". Read admin-guide request steps, agent-requests search excerpts and Package Management API overview; request listing is documented, approval/rejection calls are not.

claims.claim: Lifecycle rules are admin-opt-in rather than enforced without administrator configuration.
claims.quote:
Define the applicable criteria that determine which agent instances the rule applies to.
5. In the rule details pane, choose all agents or select a subset of agents from the list. Run the rule to apply the template.

claims.quote:

claims.where: What's changing: first paragraph; Why it matters
claims.claim: Agent management rules generally run automatically and continuously apply lifecycle policy without an administrator running them.
claims.quote:
Review impacted agents before running the rule
Apply governance actions across affected agents in bulk
The **Apply template** action is a one-time bulk operation. It isn't a scheduled rule.
claims.fix: Describe the documented experience as administrator-reviewed, rule-based bulk actions. Explicitly say Apply template is a one-time, administrator-run operation, not scheduled. Attribute automation scenarios to roadmap 481518 instead of promising all configured rules execute unattended.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: A configurable condition named 'block risky agents' exists in this rule builder.
claims.quote: Searched: "agent management rules" "risky"; Microsoft 365 agent management rules risky signals automatic deletion notification audit reassignment reverse. Read agent-settings and agent-365-overview; overview mentions risky-agent automation but no matching rule-builder condition is documented.
claims.fix: Do not present 'block risky agents' as a verified condition label. Say roadmap 481518 names risky-agent blocking, while the settings documentation lists 'Block ownerless agents without usage'; the exact risky-agent rule condition and signals are not documented there.

claims.claim: An automatic inactive-agent deletion rule is currently available on this settings page.
claims.quote: Searched: "agent management rules" "delete". Opened agent-settings, agent-actions and agent-365-overview. The settings page's supported actions omit deletion; agent-actions documents manual soft deletion, not an inactive-agent deletion rule.
claims.fix: Attribute automatic inactive-agent deletion only to the roadmap description. Explain that Learn's current supported-rule list does not document that rule, and make any inactivity/deletion-policy advice contingent on confirming the capability in the tenant.

claims.where: summary; Scope; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The manager-reassignment rule applies generally to ownerless agents across the listed platforms.
claims.quote:
#### Reassign ownerless agents created with Agent Builder to manager
This rule only supports agents created by using Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder.
claims.fix: Qualify the summary, scope and reassignment guidance: this documented rule supports Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder agents only. Do not promise manager reassignment for Copilot Studio, SharePoint, Foundry or connected-platform agents.

claims.claim: Rules support installing Microsoft agents.
claims.quote:
By using the **Install Microsoft (1P) Agents** rule, you can:
Identify Microsoft-published agents within the tenant
Review eligible agents before installation
Install selected agents for all users through a single bulk action

claims.claim: The ownerless-agent rule can transfer ownership to the previous owner's manager.
claims.quote: Transfer ownership by using a bulk reassignment action to the manager of the previous owner based on Microsoft Entra ID hierarchy

claims.claim: Rules support blocking ownerless agents that have no usage.
claims.quote: Admins can create a custom rule to block multiple ownerless agents that have no usage.

claims.claim: Rules support applying a template.
claims.quote: Use the **Apply template** action in an agent management rule to apply security policies to existing agents.

claims.claim: Rules support rejecting publish requests older than a specified number of days.
claims.quote: Admins can create a custom rule to reject multiple agent publish requests that are older than a specified number of days.

claims.claim: Administrators can install agents for users.
claims.quote: Install an agent for users so it's ready to use without manual installation by end users.

claims.claim: Administrators can uninstall previously installed agents.
claims.quote: Admin can uninstall a previously installed agent.

claims.claim: Administrators can pin agents for users.

claims.quote: However, blocking an agent that you created by using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only impacts its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Researcher and Analyst can be blocked tenant-wide but cannot be scoped through Edit users.
claims.quote: For the Researcher and Analyst agents, the **Edit users** panel is disabled. To manage their availability, block the agent for the entire tenant by using the **Block** action in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Agent risk assessments use Microsoft security signals.
claims.quote: Risk signals are sourced from: Displays the Microsoft security platforms contributing risk signals for the agent, such as Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Entra, and Microsoft Defender.
claims.fix: Cite the registry documentation and describe this as the registry's risk assessment, not proof of the undocumented risky-agent rule condition. Retain the open question about which signals that specific rule uses.

claims.claim: Reassignment grants the new owner control over the inherited agent.
claims.quote: The new owner gets full edit and delete permissions, plus access to any files the previous owner uploaded.

claims.claim: Automated deletion is irreversible for the agent definition.
claims.quote:
When you delete an agent in the Microsoft 365 admin center, the agent is soft deleted.
During the 30-day retention period, you can restore the agent or permanently delete it.
claims.fix: Replace with: 'Microsoft 365 admin center deletion is soft deletion with a 30-day recovery window; permanent deletion cannot be undone. Microsoft Learn does not establish a separate irreversible automatic-deletion rule here.'

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Blocking or deleting an agent can remove users' access.
claims.quote:
**Block and unblock** | Restrict access to an agent across the organization, preventing any user from using it.
A soft-deleted agent is unavailable to its maker and end users

claims.claim: Affected users receive no notice of blocking or deletion unless administrators add a communication step.
claims.quote: Searched: "agent management rules" "notifications" "audit"; Microsoft 365 admin center agent rules block delete notify users audit log rule changes. Read agent-settings and agent-actions; neither establishes the notification behaviour of these lifecycle rules.
claims.fix: Replace the assertion with advice: 'Plan communications for affected users; notification behaviour for these lifecycle rules is not documented in the cited pages.' Keep notification options as an open question.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance: manager attributes
claims.claim: Manager reassignment depends on the previous owner's Microsoft Entra hierarchy.
claims.quote: Transfer ownership by using a bulk reassignment action to the manager of the previous owner based on Microsoft Entra ID hierarchy

claims.claim: Agents built by departed employees keep running without an accountable owner.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 agent management rules risky signals automatic deletion notification audit reassignment reverse. Read agent-settings, agent-actions and registry ownerless-agent documentation; continued runtime after owner departure is not stated.
claims.fix: Replace with the documented narrower fact: 'Shared agents can become ownerless when their creator is deleted from the organisation, creating an ownership-governance gap.' Do not promise continued execution across agent types.

claims.claim: Unused agents remain in the store and in audit scope.
claims.quote: Searched: "agent management rules" "delete"; Microsoft 365 admin center agent rules block delete notify users audit log rule changes. Read agent-settings, agent-actions and registry documentation; no passage establishes store retention or audit scope solely from lack of usage.
claims.fix: Remove the assertion about store persistence and audit scope, or recast it as analysis: 'Review unused agents to reduce inventory and governance overhead.'

claims.claim: The admin center inventory spans Agent Builder, Copilot Studio, SharePoint, Foundry and connected platforms.
claims.quote: Specific platforms supported include: Microsoft Copilot Studio, SharePoint, Agent Builder, AI Foundry, Agents Toolkit, other Microsoft agentic types (such as Researcher), and non-Microsoft agentic platforms (such as Manus or Genspark).
claims.fix: Cite the overview. Label this as registry coverage, not a promise that every lifecycle rule supports every platform; state each rule's narrower applicability, especially Agent Builder-only manager reassignment.

claims.claim: The roadmap and checked documentation publish no government-cloud rollout dates for this item.
claims.quote: Searched: "agent management rules" "GCC" rollout date. Read roadmap 481518, agent-settings and Microsoft Agent 365 service description. No government rollout date for this item was found; the service description does list GCC availability for condition-based lifecycle actions.
claims.fix: Keep the roadmap cloud listing, but add that the current Agent 365 service description lists GCC availability for condition-based lifecycle actions. Do not let 'dates not published' imply the broader capability is unavailable in GCC.

claims.where: Governance controls: Power Platform sharing limits
claims.claim: Copilot Studio agents are generally bound by Power Platform sharing limits in their home environment.
claims.quote:
You configure the sharing limits for agents as a Managed Environments control in the Power Platform admin center.
Sharing limits only apply to agents that require authentication.
claims.fix: Qualify the sentence: 'For authenticated Copilot Studio agents in Managed Environments, configured Power Platform sharing limits govern new sharing operations; existing access is not retroactively removed.' Cite this sharing-controls page.

claims.where: Governance controls: Power Platform data policies
claims.claim: Power Platform data policies also govern Copilot Studio agents.
claims.quote: **Use Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies** in Copilot Studio to block publishing agents through Copilot Studio supported channels.

claims.claim: A change record of these rule configurations can be reconstructed from the audit log.
claims.quote: Searched: "agent management rules" "notifications" "audit"; site:learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-log-activities "rule" "agent". Read agent-settings and the Agent Management audit-activities search excerpt; no rule-definition or rule-configuration audit payload is established.
claims.fix: Remove the promise that audit logs provide a rule change record. Recommend recording rule definitions and changes manually until Microsoft documents the specific rule-configuration events and payloads; distinguish documented agent-action events from rule-definition history.

claims.claim: Agent blocking and deletion events can be used in a change log.
claims.quote:
| Blocked Agent | BlockedAgent | An admin blocked an agent. Users in the organization can't use the agent. |
| Deleted Agent | DeletedAgent | An admin deleted a shared agent that deletes the underlying files and the agent. |
claims.fix: Cite this audit-activities reference. Describe these as documented administrative action events, not verified evidence that every automated rule execution or rule-definition change is logged with reconstructable details.

claims.claim: The controls table covers the filters and lifecycle actions the governance checklist asks administrators to use.
claims.quote:
Run the **Missing an owner** and **Availability: No users** filters
Start with reassignment of ownerless agents
The table lists rules, manual block/unblock, agent access and publish requests, but not the inventory filters or manual reassignment/deletion controls.
claims.fix: Add an agent-inventory review row covering the two documented filters. Where manual reassignment or deletion remains in the checklist, add their documented controls from agent-actions, or clearly make the advice conditional on the corresponding documented rule.

claims.claim: The ownerless-agent manager reassignment is reversible.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 agent management rules risky signals automatic deletion notification audit reassignment reverse. Read agent-settings, agent-actions and copilotPackage: reassign; ownership transfer is documented, but undoing this rule or restoring a departed original owner is not.
claims.fix: Remove '(reversible)'. If useful, say that administrators can perform a further ownership reassignment for eligible shared agents, without promising an undo operation for the manager-reassignment rule.
